title: Inter-region rate-limiter starvation during reserved-pool migration causing customer throttles
creator: Marco Liu
description:
Summary: During a scheduled reserved-pool migration (AZ -> cross-region rebalancing) a combination of per-region rate-limiter token buckets and an async metadata sync for burst allowances produced a transient capacity shortfall. Multiple Dedicated customers experienced higher-than-expected throttling for 6-18 minutes while the system reconciled burst allowances, leading to escalations from two customers on paid Dedicated contracts.

Why this is novel: Existing incidents have centered on headroom miscalculation and autoscaler timing. This issue stems from asymmetric accounting between global burst credits (globally allocated per-tenant) and local enforcement by per-region rate limiters during pool movement — a race combined with a delayed metadata refresh from the migration controller. The result is fast path requests hit local token buckets that have not been topped up even though global credits were present.

Impact: Elevated 429/503 responses for affected tenants, increased customer-support tickets, degraded P95 latency spikes due to retry storms, and two escalations from enterprise customers requesting immediate remediation and root-cause analysis.
timeline: 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC - Automated migration job started to rebalance reserved pools between us-east-1 and us-west-2
2026-03-10 02:13 UTC - Canary traffic observed 10x throttling against local rate limiter; Pager alerted on surge in 429s for dedicated tier
2026-03-10 02:16 UTC - On-call mobilized (Aisha). Initial mitigation: paused migration job and manually forced metadata sync to regional rate limiter services
2026-03-10 02:20 UTC - Temporary hotfix applied: instruct per-region rate limiter to accept global burst tokens for affected tenants (feature flag enable) — immediate reduction in 429s
2026-03-10 02:40 UTC - Confirmed customer-facing errors subsided; migration resumed with conservative shuffle settings and enhanced observability
2026-03-11 09:00 UTC - Post-incident investigation started; reproduced locally with synthetic migration and race window narrowing
2026-03-14 14:30 UTC - Proposed long-term fix and PR drafted (see links)
findings: Per-region token buckets enforce burst limits using locally cached 'allowance' metadata refreshed asynchronously from the global accounting service
Migration controller updates burst ownership and pool assignment first in global store, then notifies region services; under heavy concurrency the notification can be delayed by multiple seconds

During that delay, local rate limiters continue to enforce older local allowance values, which can be zero for tenants that were just moved into the region, causing immediate throttles despite global credit availability
Autoscaler decisions and pool draining logic assume instantaneous metadata propagation and therefore schedule capacity transfers that create temporary enforcement gaps
Retries from upstream clients amplify load to fallback regions, causing higher P95 latencies and brief overloads on nearby pools
mitigation_steps: Hotfix (rolled at 02:20 UTC): Enabled 'global-burst-accept' feature flag in region services to temporarily allow trusted global burst tokens until local caches refresh
Paused the migration job to prevent additional race windows
Manual metadata push to all affected regional rate-limiter caches to reconcile allowances
Customer comms: Notified impacted tenants, opened incident bridges, and provided ETA for fix; two account managers engaged directly
root_cause: Architecture mismatch: global accounting + async local enforcement created a small but impactful race window during pool migrations
Migration controller did not await acknowledgment from regional enforcement services before shifting active traffic
No fallback path that treats global burst credits as authoritative during reconciliation windows
code_changes: PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1459 - add authoritative-global-credit-read-through to per-region rate limiter
PR: github.com/redwood-inference/controller/pull/298 - migration controller waits for regional ack or times out with conservative rollback
Feature flag: global-burst-accept (default off) implemented for controlled rollouts
qa_and_repro_steps: 1) Start a synthetic reserved-pool migration in staging that moves tenant T across regions
2) Ensure per-region rate-limiter cache is cold for tenant T (clear cache or start with zero allowance)
3) Apply controlled burst traffic from tenant T to exceed local bucket while global credits exist
4) Observe 429s when local bucket is enforced before metadata sync; enable global-burst-accept to verify acceptance path
5) Capture telemetry: per-region allowance refresh times, migration controller acknowledgments, and retry amplification metrics
postmortem_actions: Short term (next 72h): Roll feature-flag to all regions for trusted customers, add migration safety window (default 30s) and notify PMs/SEs
Medium term (2 weeks): Ship PRs linked above; add end-to-end test coverage for migration + rate-limiter enforcement and include chaos tests
Long term (quarter): Rework metadata propagation to use push+ack protocol or strong-consistency check for critical burst fields; update runbooks
Operational: Add dashboard panels showing metadata drift between global store and regional caches and alert when drift > 500ms
next_steps: Merge PRs and schedule canary rollout in staging and prod with telemetry gates
Coordinate with SEs to identify enterprise customers that had throttling and validate post-deploy behavior
Draft a public-facing incident summary for affected customers and include timeline and mitigations
Update migration controller to require regional ack or fallback to conservative placement when ack fails
comments: 2026-03-11 - Samantha Ortiz: Reviewed findings; agree that push+ack is safest. Recommend temporary feature-flag rollout for critical tenants only.
2026-03-12 - DevOps (Ravi Patel): We saw a 3-5s median metadata diff between global store and region caches during the job window; adding alerting now.
2026-03-13 - Aisha Banerjee: Hotfix verified in prod for impacted regions. Preparing canary plan for full rollout next week.
2026-03-14 - Paul Nguyen (Support Eng): Two customers confirmed reduction in throttles after hotfix; collecting logs for audit
